description.text: Eros is the Greek god of physical love and desire, known in Latin as Cupido. In the earliest Greek sources he is a primordial deity, the fourth being created after Chaos, Gaia, and Tartarus, according to Hesiod.

Later myths portray him as the son of Aphrodite and Ares, and he is often depicted as a youthful figure with a bow and arrow or as an adult holding a lyre. Eros is linked to athletics, is considered a protector of homosexual love, and is frequently shown with dolphins, flutes, roosters, roses, and torches.

curiosities.text: In Athens the fourth day of every month was dedicated to Eros, reflecting his importance in the city’s religious calendar.
A fertility cult of Eros existed at Tespie, where he was worshipped in a context distinct from that of Aphrodite.
Orphic cosmogonies describe Eros emerging from Nyx (Night) and as the first divine being to generate the cosmos, positioning him as a foundational figure in the creation myth.
